idiom_name: errgroup.Group fan-out over a results slice + errors.Join for accumulation
implementation_notes: Go has no higher-kinded types, so no generic Applicative interface is expressible; the idiomatic realization is a fan-out where each independent computation runs in its own g.Go closure and writes into a pre-sized results slice, followed by g.Wait(). What replaces the classic structure is the join itself: errgroup plus a result slice pairs the values, and errors.Join(errs...) (Go 1.20+) accumulates the failures - with generics (Go 1.18) a Result[T] can carry value and error together. The classic applicative form is justified when several independent inputs must be validated together; a single error-returning function chain is fail-fast and simpler when only the first problem matters.
pitfalls: Returning a non-nil error from a g.Go closure puts the group in fail-fast mode (and cancels a context-scoped group): accumulation requires appending to a shared error slice and returning nil.
Appending to a shared slice from goroutines is a data race without a mutex; writing to distinct indices of a pre-sized slice is safe, which is why the results slice is sized up front.
errors.Join loses the identity of individual errors for errors.As/Is unless callers unwrap the joined error; if structured errors matter, keep the []error slice in the result instead of joining.
Goroutines keep running after the first failure: without cancellation or a wait policy, the accumulation path does the same work twice as a fail-fast path that cancels.
